summary: This standards-track RFC defines a new L2TPv3 Attribute-Value Pair letting L2TP Control Connection Endpoints advertise one or more S-BFD Discriminator values.

eli5.summary: Tunnel endpoints tell each other their S-BFD identifiers by a new field in L2TPv3 messages.

questions: what is the s-bfd target discriminator id avp
how does l2tpv3 advertise s-bfd discriminators
subtitle: A new L2TPv3 AVP lets tunnel endpoints advertise the S-BFD discriminators they will answer to.

tldr.problem: Seamless BFD needs every node to know the discriminators other nodes have reserved for it, and L2TPv3 is one possible way to share them.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7886 defines the S-BFD Target Discriminator ID AVP (Attribute Type 102), carrying one or more 4-octet discriminators in ICRQ, ICRP, OCRQ and OCRP messages.
tldr.outcome: An endpoint can announce that it runs an S-BFD reflector, and a peer that wants to monitor connectivity can use the values. A peer that does not care can safely ignore the AVP.

today: RFC 7886 is a Proposed Standard, published in July 2016, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 7880 defines a simplified use of Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (RFC 5880) called Seamless BFD (S-BFD). It depends on network nodes knowing the BFD discriminators that each node has reserved for this purpose, and it requires unique discriminators within an administrative domain.

The Layer Two Tunneling Protocol version 3 (RFC 3931) is one possible means of advertising those discriminators. This document specifies the encoding to use when it is done.
sections.eli5: Nodes need to know each other's special numbers to check that a link is alive. This RFC says how tunnel endpoints can share those numbers.

sections.title: Assumed Background
sections.content:
The reader is expected to be very familiar with S-BFD terminology (Section 2 of RFC 7880) and L2TPv3 constructs (Section 1.3 of RFC 3931). The RFC uses the RFC 2119 key words such as MUST and MAY in their usual meaning.

An LCCE is an L2TP Control Connection Endpoint, one end of an L2TP control connection. An AVP (Attribute Value Pair) is the unit L2TP control messages use to carry a piece of information.
sections.eli5: You should already know what S-BFD and L2TP are. This RFC only adds one small piece.

sections.title: The S-BFD Target Discriminator ID AVP
sections.content:
The AVP has Attribute Type 102. It is exchanged in the ICRQ (Incoming-Call-Request), ICRP (Incoming-Call-Reply), OCRQ (Outgoing-Call-Request) and OCRP (Outgoing-Call-Reply) control messages during session negotiation.

The Attribute Value field holds the discriminator values, 4 octets per discriminator, with at least one required. The AVP says the advertiser implements an S-BFD reflector for the listed target discriminators and is ready for reflector operation. The M bit of the L2TP control message MUST NOT be set inside this AVP.
sections.eli5: The AVP is a small label with a list of numbers. Each number takes up the same fixed space, four bytes.

sections.title: How Endpoints Use It
sections.content:
An LCCE MAY include the AVP in ICRQ, ICRP, OCRQ or OCRP. The receiving LCCE MAY use it if it wants to monitor connectivity to the advertiser with S-BFD. If it does not, it MAY safely discard the AVP without affecting the rest of session negotiation.

When one discriminator is advertised, it is associated with the L2TPv3 session. Several MAY be included, and the encoding allows any number for extensibility, although RFC 7880 deals with only one discriminator unless a mapping to entities is specified. How multiple discriminators map to a specific use case is out of scope.
sections.eli5: You can wear the name tag with one number or several. If nobody needs it, they just ignore it and the introductions go on fine.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: IANA maintains the Control Message Attribute Value Pairs sub-registry under RFC 3438. IANA has assigned value 102 to the S-BFD Target Discriminator ID.
sections.eli5: The official list of label numbers now has number 102 reserved for this label.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: Security for L2TP is covered by RFC 3931, and the new AVP introduces no new security risks for L2TP. However, advertising discriminators makes it possible for attackers to start S-BFD sessions using the advertised information. The vulnerabilities and mitigations are discussed in the Security Considerations of RFC 7880.
sections.eli5: Sharing your extension means a stranger could dial it, so the S-BFD rules explain how to guard against that.
